generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a running bamboo 4 to 9 m tall that spreads from its rhizomes into dense groves of straight, yellow-green culms 2 to 5 cm thick, each reaching its full height within a few weeks of emerging and living about seven years, leafy above with sprays of narrow leaves at its nodes. A woody grass whose culms live for years, so its growth form is shrub. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 6.5 m at 6 years and 7 m at 15. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: yellow-green culms, fresh green leaves.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.culm_length_m.note: Hitchcock (p. 31): P. aurea is frequent in cultivation, the plant 3 to 5 m tall, its branches yellowish and its lower internodes very short. GrassBase (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read) gives culms 200 to 800 cm, so the greatest is 8 m.

traits.stem_diameter_max_m.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): culms erect, 200-800 cm long, 20-30 mm in diameter, woody, internodes hollow, 8-10 cm long.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): rhizomes elongated, leptomorph (running). See disagreements: Bureau 1904 found it only slightly running in Paris.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): leaf-blades lanceolate, 5-8 cm long, 5-11 mm wide (AusGrass, also as search results quote it, gives 5-15 cm by 5-22 mm).

traits.leaf_width_m.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): leaf-blades 5-11 mm wide.

traits.spikelet_length_m.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): spikelets sessile, lanceolate, 18-25 mm long.

traits.florets_per_spikelet.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): spikelets of 2 fertile florets with a barren rachilla extension.

traits.lemma_length_m.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): fertile lemma ovate, about 15 mm long.
